highlights: No declared harmonization: the cumulative is cleanly additive (2973 + 102 = 3075; 1309 + 45 = 1354).

alerts_total.data_gap_note: Tableau 3 (at 24/07): 1937 alerts of the day (1858 new + 79 Report-J-1) across Ituri, Nord-Kivu, Haut-Uele and Tshopo; Sud-Kivu is ND on every row and excluded rather than counted as zero. Province rows sum exactly (866+977+45+49 = 1937 reported; 641+948+4+24 = 1617 investigated; 135+44+2+8 = 189 living; 63+20+1+1 = 85 community deaths; 198+64+3+9 = 274 suspects, and 189 + 85 = 274). ITURI RECOVERED SHARPLY: 53.8% -> 74.0% (641/866), breaking a six-cycle decline (86.4 -> 75.6 -> 72.8 -> 66.7 -> 64.0 -> 53.8 -> 74.0) and doing so on a much larger volume (550 -> 866 reported), which makes the recovery harder to explain as a denominator effect. Nord-Kivu holds at 97.0%. Haut-Uele returns to the alert table and immediately reports the worst rate on the surface, 8.9% (4 of 45), with 40 of those 45 carried from the previous day; Tshopo fell to 48.9%. The national 83.5% is up from 79.8% and this cycle it moves WITH the epicentre rather than against it.

challenges.finding: Reticence toward post-mortem sampling (EDS/swabs), community resistance and insecurity targeting EDS teams delay confirmation and under-estimate cases.
challenges.response: Intensify CREC/RCCE, involve religious and community leaders, secure the teams and increase the number of EDS teams.

challenges.finding: Eight health zones (Bambu, Gety, Damas, Lolwa, Mahagi, Rimba, Masereka, Mutwanga) had no contact data at consolidation, so Ituri and Nord-Kivu follow-up rates cover reporting zones only.
challenges.response: Restore reporting from the missing zones before reading any follow-up trend.

challenges.finding: Insufficient CTE/CT capacity: occupancy 126.9% in Nord-Kivu (141 beds) and 81.2% in Ituri (576 patients for 709 beds), raising admission delays and nosocomial transmission risk.
challenges.response: Accelerate CTE construction and expansion, deploy temporary structures and report bed capacity systematically.

challenges.finding: Isolation escapes doubled to 8 in 24 hours (Ituri 7, Nord-Kivu 1), the highest single-cycle figure of the recent series.
challenges.response: Reinforce isolation-site security, psychosocial support and patient-family liaison.

challenges.finding: Haut-Uele continues to grow (29 -> 35 confirmed, 15 -> 19 deaths across five zones) and high mobility raises the risk of urban, riverine and cross-border diffusion.
challenges.response: Activate the priority PoE/PoC in Haut-Uele and reinforce cross-border coordination.

challenges.finding: Insecurity and limited access (CODECO, ADF) restrict operations.
challenges.response: Reinforce security coordination and humanitarian access.

challenges.finding: Continuity of essential (non-Ebola) health services is compromised, raising indirect mortality.
challenges.response: Effective implementation of free care and reinforcement of essential-service continuity.

contacts_total.data_gap_note: Tableau 4 (24 July): 14525 under follow-up, 11100 seen, 76.4% national, still far below the 95% operational threshold. Province rows sum exactly (10123+4111+258+33 = 14525; 7466+3418+186+30 = 11100). CRITICAL DENOMINATOR CHANGE, flagged by the source's own asterisk: in Ituri and Nord-Kivu the follow-up rate is computed ONLY over health zones that reported. Bambu, Gety, Damas, Lolwa, Mahagi, Rimba, Masereka and Mutwanga had no data at consolidation. Ituri's cohort therefore SHRANK 11332 -> 10123 (-1209) while its rate rose 72.1% -> 73.8%, so the improvement is not comparable to earlier cycles and must not be read as recovered field performance; the same caveat applies to Nord-Kivu's 78.9% -> 83.1% on a cohort that grew 4001 -> 4111. Haut-Uele reports contact follow-up for the FIRST time (186/258 = 72.1%), which is a genuine coverage gain, and Tshopo's small cohort moved 25 -> 33 at 90.9%. Sud-Kivu remains closed (0/0, NA). Note that 'Mutwanga' appears in the source's non-reporting list but is not on the 48-zone affected roster; it is preserved as printed and not added to the roster.

patient_movement_total.data_gap_note: SitRep71 Tableau 6 end-of-day census 755 at 88.8% occupancy (755/850 beds): Ituri 576 @81.2% (709 beds, 275 confirmed / 301 suspected), Nord-Kivu 179 @126.9% (141 beds, 16 / 163); Haut-Uele AND Tshopo both report ND. The confirmed/suspect split closes exactly (291 + 464 = 755, and each reporting province closes: Ituri 275+301 = 576, Nord-Kivu 16+163 = 179). The bed identity closes exactly (756 J-1 + 113 admissions - 114 exits = 755). Exits over 24h (114 total): 16 deaths, 74 non-cases, 16 recoveries, 8 escapes, 0 HGR transfers. Nord-Kivu EASED 136.2% -> 126.9% on unchanged 141 beds (192 -> 179 patients) but remains the only province over capacity. Ituri bed capacity is flat at 709 for a third consecutive cycle while its occupancy rose 80.4% -> 81.2%. National capacity FELL 860 -> 850 beds because Tshopo dropped out of bed reporting (it held 10 beds last cycle), so the occupancy move 89.1% -> 88.8% is partly a composition effect. ESCAPES DOUBLED to 8 (Ituri 7, Nord-Kivu 1) from 4, the highest single-cycle figure in the recent series; escapes are a period flow and are summed across cycles, never carried as a stock.

priorities.priority: Restore contact reporting in the eight non-reporting health zones (Bambu, Gety, Damas, Lolwa, Mahagi, Rimba, Masereka, Mutwanga). Ituri's follow-up rate rose 72.1% -> 73.8% only because its cohort shrank by 1209 contacts; the rate is computed over reporting zones alone and is not comparable to earlier cycles. Treat the apparent improvement as unproven until the cohort is whole.

Consolidate the Ituri alert-investigation recovery (53.8% -> 74.0% on volume up 550 -> 866), the first improvement after six consecutive declines, and address Haut-Uele's 8.9% (4 of 45, 40 carried from J-1) now that the province is back in the alert table with five affected zones.

Sustain the Nord-Kivu easing (136.2% -> 126.9% on unchanged 141 beds) while it remains the only province over capacity, and restore ND bed reporting in Haut-Uele and Tshopo, whose withdrawal cut national capacity 860 -> 850.
Investigate the doubling of isolation escapes to 8 in 24h (Ituri 7, Nord-Kivu 1), the highest single-cycle figure in the recent series and a direct transmission risk.
Community deaths were 36 of 45 confirmed deaths (80.0%), the highest share of the recent series, with Ituri at 29 of 35 (82.9%). The post-mortem share of confirmations was 36 of 102 (35.3%).

Testing volume recovered 278 -> 381 analyzed (+37%). Sustain the newly inaugurated Kasenyi laboratory (Tchomia, Ituri) and restore a Haut-Uele block: its six notified cases again have no laboratory line.

preserved_conflicts: SitRep71 national headline is DRC-only (3075 confirmed / 1354 confirmed deaths across five provinces); the country-scope snapshot adds the Uganda component (20/2/11) separately -> 3095 confirmed / 1356 deaths / 567 recovered. Uganda MoH reports no new cases through 2026-07-24 against a cumulative of 20 (last positive 2026-06-21), so the anchor is carried unchanged on a confirmed rather than an assumed basis.

NO HARMONIZATION this cycle. The cumulative is cleanly additive (2973 + 102 = 3075; 1309 + 45 = 1354) and the count-reconciliation gate classifies both metrics as reconciled with a zero gap, so this boundary IS safe to difference for trend work.

CONTACT-TRACING DENOMINATOR: the source's own asterisk states that Ituri and Nord-Kivu follow-up rates were computed only for health zones that reported, with Bambu, Gety, Damas, Lolwa, Mahagi, Rimba, Masereka and Mutwanga missing at consolidation. Ituri's cohort shrank 11332 -> 10123 while its rate rose 72.1% -> 73.8%. The rate is preserved as printed but is NOT comparable to earlier cycles.

'Mutwanga' appears in the source's non-reporting-zone footnote but is not among the 48 affected health zones on the page-1 roster or in Tableau 2. It is preserved as printed and is NOT added to the affected roster.

COHORT ARITHMETIC DOES NOT SUPPORT THE STATED EXPLANATION. The source attributes the Ituri follow-up figure to eight non-reporting zones, but the six Ituri members of that list (Bambu, Gety, Damas, Lolwa, Mahagi, Rimba) carry only 83 of Ituri's 2733 cumulative confirmed cases = 3.0% of the provincial caseload, while the cohort fell 11332 -> 10123 = 10.7%. Those zones are near-dormant (Gety 1 case, Mahagi 2, Lolwa 4, Rimba 8, Damas 14, Bambu 54 with +3 this cycle); even a generous contacts-per-case ratio puts them at a few hundred contacts, not 1209. Most of the drop is therefore UNEXPLAINED by the footnote. Two facts bound the reading: contacts track recent rather than cumulative cases, so caseload share is an imperfect proxy; and the Ituri cohort is inherently volatile, with cycle deltas spanning -2239 to +2384 (mean +132), so -1209 ranks only 5th most negative of 43 observed transitions. CONCLUSION: the 72.1% -> 73.8% movement is UNINTERPRETABLE this cycle, not an improvement. Per-zone contact denominators are not published, so this cannot be resolved from the SitRep alone.

The day's laboratory positives (87 + 9 + 0 = 96) fall six short of the day's 102 confirmations because Haut-Uele reports no laboratory block for its six notified cases; the identity holds at 96 + 6 = 102. Preserved rather than forced.

Haut-Uele and Tshopo both report ND for bed capacity this cycle. Tshopo held 10 beds at SitRep70, so national capacity falls 860 -> 850 and the occupancy move 89.1% -> 88.8% is partly a composition effect rather than pure decompression.
Rwampara advances +25 confirmed with a ZERO death day column (community 0, intra-CTE 0), so its cumulative deaths hold at 236 and its CFR falls 48.2% -> 45.8% on denominator growth alone.

The section-3.1 alert narrative again describes the movement as an improvement reflecting reduced investigation carry-over. This cycle that reading is broadly supported for Ituri (53.8% -> 74.0%) but not for Haut-Uele (8.9%) or Tshopo (86.7% -> 48.9%); the printed rates are promoted.
